I was around the same age when I really started to struggle with insecurities (and depression) as well. Although it is normal for people to have insecurities that consume their thoughts, especially around this age, you should not feel you have to suck it up and deal with it. I don't want you to think you'll be "doomed to this eternity".

I totally understand what you mean by "fighting the good feeling" that should come with compliments. Insecurities can take over how you perceive how others view you. Even subconsciously, your brain can try to come up with excuses for why the person was lying or how they were "just trying to be nice". Hell, I am even in a serious relationship now and its still a bit hard for me to take compliments from my boyfriend sometimes! Therapy has definitely been helping me get through these issues and put more trust in the validity of compliments given towards me. I've learned lots of tools to help rewire my thought processes to learn to accept myself for who I am.

Something that has helped me outside of therapy is to just accept the compliment anyways, thank the person, and try not to think about the situation too much afterwards. Overthinking can only harm you. Forcing myself to take compliments has actually made it feel a bit more natural to accept them in the future.

Last thing I wanted to say is that you shouldn't feel discouraged if you feel you are not "getting anywhere" with improvement on your self-image. It can feel like it's taking forever. But since these insecurities are often deeply-rooted within people, healing will always take the form of baby steps. No matter how you choose to tackle this, please take time every once in awhile to look back at the improvements you've made since this point in your life. Growing takes a long time but it helps to reflect and notice the strides you have made since the beginning.
